COURT OF APPEAL OF THE STATE OF WESTBROOK, DIVISION TWO

PEOPLE v. ANTOINE J. BARRETT          No. A-160-2024-CR

RESPONDENT'S BRIEF (Excerpts)

ARGUMENT (in opposition):

I. THE ANONYMOUS TIP, COMBINED WITH OFFICER OBSERVATIONS, SUPPLIED REASONABLE SUSPICION TO STOP AND PROBABLE CAUSE TO SEARCH UNDER THE AUTOMOBILE EXCEPTION.

This case is not Florida v. J.L. In J.L., officers stopped the suspect on the tip alone with no independent observation. Here, Trooper Reeves observed Appellant and followed him for over two miles. The trooper testified that Appellant "seemed nervous," supplying corroboration of the tip's predictive value.

Under California v. Acevedo, 500 U.S. 565 (1991), once probable cause to search a vehicle exists, no warrant is required.

II. THE TRIAL COURT CORRECTLY ADMITTED THE STATEMENT BECAUSE APPELLANT VOLUNTARILY LIMITED HIS INVOCATION TO THE INSTANT OFFENSE.

A defendant may waive Miranda rights selectively. McNeil v. Wisconsin, 501 U.S. 171 (1991). Appellant's invocation was, by its own terms, limited to questions "about the drugs in my car." Questions about the 2021 incident were not within the scope of the invocation.

(Remainder omitted.)

Dated: August 6, 2024
                                /s/ M. Powell, Senior ADA
                                For the People of Westbrook
